newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: INSTANT VIEW - NZ GDP data weaker than expected.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - NZ GDP data weaker than expected.

text.p: Following are economists' immediate views on the March GDP data from New Zealand which showed a seasonally-adjusted 0.5 percent fall.
ASB CHIEF ECONOMIST ANTHONY BYETT

"It appears the economy was a little weaker than expected by both the Reserve Bank and the treasury so I would expect a small rally (in interest rates) and a lower New Zealand dollar as a result, but it's probably too close to the RB's monetary policy statement to mean anything more than that."
PAUL STEWART, CHIEF ECONOMIST AT ANZ BANK
"A fairly weak number, and at this stage we wouldn't discount the possibility of another negative number in June.
"Obviously it supports the view that economic activity is fairly soft.
"Dare I say it, Treasury's forecasts for next year will be difficult to achieve.
"If we continue to see a run of weaker activity and inflation data, then the market might look to price in even greater amounts of easing.
"I'll need to have a closer look at the figures, but at this stage in terms of the balance of risk and the bias, then that market reaction would be appropriate.
"But I'd be cautious about saying that it's going change the Reserve Bank's view too much at this stage. I still think the next key figure is the June quarter CPI."
PETER JOLLY, ECONOMIST AT BNZ BANK
"Pretty low. It was even lower than we thought and considerably lower than what the market, and more particularly the Reserve Bank, thought.
"It has to be positive for interest rates.
"Now that we've got this 50-point (comfort) band from the Reserve Bank, we're just going to bash on the bottom of that for the next couple of weeks.
"It's unlikely that the Reserve Bank will widen that band in the face of this number.
"Perhaps the market can't take short rates down much further, but it can tend to build any further easing into the shorter-dated bonds and the like."
BANKERS TRUST CHIEF ECONOMISTS DAVID PLANK
Called the data weaker than forecasts, so he also expected markets over the coming weeks to test the bottom of the Reserve Bank's comfort zone.

While there were some technical explanations for the weak number -- fewer trading days for example -- Plank said he expected growth over the March and June quarters was likely to be less than both the treasury and the central bank had forecast.
"That will, over time, encourage the market to ease conditions through the bottom of the Reserve Bank's current comfort zone," he said.
Plank expected upcoming retail sales data to again confirm the trough in economic conditions.
"The market, maybe not this week but over the coming weeks, will move through that 775 point zone. If the data is weak enough I don't think the Reserve bank will stand in their way."
-- Wellington newsroom 64 4 4734 746
